> NEXORA is a compact PC control deck with a small OLED touchscreen and a modern, futuristic design. It makes everyday PC tasks easier by putting your favorite shortcuts and controls all in one place. It features 9 customizable shortcut buttons that let you open apps, launch games, run macros, access folders, and perform quick actions on your PC with a single tap. You can set up each button to do whatever works best for you. The OLED screen gives you quick access to your shortcuts and different control panels. You can also use it to manage things like system volume, microphone settings, and other useful PC functions. NEXORA also includes a dedicated Spotify section, letting you play or pause music, skip tracks, and control your playback without having to switch windows. There's also an optional speaker output feature that lets you play Spotify audio through a connected speaker. The idea behind NEXORA is simple: make your PC easier to control, keep your favorite tools close at hand, and give you a setup that looks as good as it works.

## Design

### 2026-10-11 – At the beginning of this session, I spent about 2 hours researching how to start the project. I read the introduction and the getting-started guide carefully, then I began looking for all the material

**2h**

At the beginning of this session, I spent about 2 hours researching how to start the project. I read the introduction and the getting-started guide carefully, then I began looking for all the materials I need for NEXORA, my ESP32-S3 macro pad. I put together a complete shopping list: an ESP32-S3 dev board for prototyping, a 2.42" SSD1309 OLED screen, MX switches, hot-swap sockets, diodes, a rotary encoder, a USB-C connector, and the passive components for the PCB.

### 2026-10-11 – I also started learning how soldering works, since I will need to solder the components onto my PCB later. I watched tutorials to understand the basic technique, how to use a soldering iron, solder an

**2h**

I also started learning how soldering works, since I will need to solder the components onto my PCB later. I watched tutorials to understand the basic technique, how to use a soldering iron, solder and flux, and how to avoid common mistakes like cold joints. On top of that, I studied the different types of components in my project, such as resistors, capacitors, diodes, voltage regulators, and tactile switches, to understand what each one does and why it is needed in the circuit.
